literal: Virtue as called-indeed [is] domestic life; that-even, another-person blaming without-if, [is] good.
translation: Domestic life is indeed what is called virtue. Even that is truly good only if it is free from the reproach of others.
modern: அறம் என்று சிறப்பித்துச் சொல்லப்படுவது குடும்ப வாழ்க்கையே ஆகும். அந்த வாழ்க்கையும் மற்றவர்கள் பழிக்கும்படி இல்லாமல் இருந்தால் மிகவும் நல்லது.
explanation: This couplet defines true virtue as living a good domestic life. The phrase 'aṟaṉ eṉappaṭṭatē' emphasizes that family life itself is the very definition of virtue. However, it adds a crucial condition: 'aḵtum' (even that) is only truly good ('naṉṟu') if it is lived without giving cause for others to blame or reproach ('piṟaṉ paḻippatu illāyiṉ'). The word 'aṟaṉ' is a variant of 'aṟam' (virtue), chosen here for metrical harmony.
